scenario: In-flight GA execution outlives the runtime-task lease (honest failure + lease expiry)

ledger.note: the interrupted model call is retained as UNKNOWN; it was NOT replayed and the budget was NOT reset

rootCause.finding: RuntimeTaskScheduler.heartbeat() has no caller anywhere in production code; no scheduled lease-renewal task exists; spec.agent.execution.heartbeat-seconds is only read/written, never consumed.
rootCause.designReference: PHASE1_MULTI_WORKER_EXECUTION_DESIGN.md §6.4 requires an independent bounded heartbeat executor that must not use the model-call thread pool.
rootCause.consequence: Any execution whose wall-clock duration exceeds lease-seconds is recovered as LEASE_EXPIRED and terminalized with EXECUTION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, even while the worker process is healthy and actively streaming. Defaults (lease 60s) still fail for real inference exceeding 60s; the documented 180s GA execution fence cannot be honoured with real providers.
rootCause.secondaryFinding: All @Scheduled tasks share Spring Boot's default single-thread scheduler, so a blocking execution also starves the cross-instance SSE catch-up poller on the executing instance.

stillValidEvidence: Live in-flight SSE delivery from the peer API: the B-subscription received sequence 4 and 5 after reconnect/catch-up while the run was still executing (see cross-instance scenario output)
limitations: The executing Worker identity vs the SSE-serving JVM identity was not yet confirmed for this run; the peer subscription is not yet recorded as cross-instance catch-up evidence
This is a reproduced defect, not an accepted behaviour; a fix and a regression test are required
